paras: The 35th and Wabash police shooting took place on the evening of August 20, 1920, in Chicago, when a white policeman described as drunk fired at a Black man after a traffic quarrel at 35th Street and Wabash Avenue. The shots missed, the man disarmed the officer, and a second policeman had him taken away. Two Chicago Black weeklies reported it the next day; the Chicago Whip said he "came near causing a riot."

The Chicago Defender named the officer as Hence, star No. 1140, third precinct, while the Whip called him "Bennesy (white)," a sergeant. In the Defender's account, the quarrel began over the right of way on Wabash, and a white man in the officer's rear seat struck the Black man, who struck back. The Whip instead had the officer weaving east on 35th Street, forcing an oncoming car to stall, then firing two shots at its driver as he cranked the engine.

Both papers said the shots missed; the Defender added that they also missed women and children. According to the Defender the man threw the gun into the crowd and gave the officer "a good thrashing"; the Whip said the pistol went over a fence. Officer Helser, on crossing duty a block away, then arrived; the Whip spelled the name Heiser and called him a "Colored Policeman."

The Defender said the officer was carried by patrol to the station at 24th and Cottage Grove. The Whip reported that he used "extremely vile language" about the colored witnesses, that the police blotter showed no record of his arrest, and that it had reported the affair to the Chief of Police. No report of charges or discipline appears in the coverage.

Only Chicago's Black weeklies carried the incident, both on August 21; no white-press report was found. The Defender ran it under the subhead "Drunken Cop Fires Gun at Citizen" at the end of a front-page story on streetcar conductors. The Whip's front-page story credited the Black officer, mocked the shooter as a "whiskey-head cop," and said the driver "properly disarmed" him.
The accounts differ on the officer's name, his direction, whether a passenger struck first, and where the gun went; both are same-day local reports without named sources.

reader.title: 35th and Wabash police shooting
bases: Both accounts describe a single policeman, said to be drunk, firing at a Black man after a traffic quarrel; no mob attacked anyone (A1, A2).

Two separate Chicago Black weeklies of the same day independently report a drunken white officer firing at a man at 35th and Wabash, being disarmed, and being taken away by a second officer, though details differ (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Chicago Defender
accounts.gist: A right-of-way quarrel on Wabash Avenue; a white man in the officer's rear seat struck the Black man, who struck back; the officer fired, missed, and was disarmed and thrashed; Helser had him taken to the station.

accounts.label: Chicago Whip
accounts.gist: The officer, driving east on 35th Street in a police flivver, forced an oncoming car to stall, then came back and fired two shots at its driver as he cranked it; the driver disarmed him and threw the pistol over a fence; Heiser sent him to the cooler but no arrest was recorded.

framing.detail: Defender headline "Drunken Cop Fires Gun at Citizen"; calls the officer 'the drunken officer' and the man 'a member of the Race' who gave him 'a good thrashing'.

Whip headline "Prompt Action of Colored Policeman Averts Trouble"; calls the officer a 'whiskey-head cop' and 'disgraced minion of the law', says the driver 'properly disarmed' him, and notes the missing blotter record.

conflicts.note: The Defender gives a star number; the Whip hedges its name ('claimed').

versions.value: Right-of-way dispute going south on Wabash; a white man in the officer's rear seat struck the Black man first
Officer driving east on 35th forced another car to stall, then returned and fired at its driver as he cranked his car
